name: Diagonal Plaza (opened as Hawthorn Court)
headline: Boulder Housing Partners, the City of Boulder's housing authority, built a 73-unit, two-building family community on a former Diagonal Plaza parking lot in north-central Boulder with a $1,450,000-a-year 2023 Round One 9% credit award from CHFA; it opened as Hawthorn Court, with residents moving in by the end of August 2025.
why_it_matters: It shows a housing authority turning a market-rate developer's inclusionary housing obligation into a free land donation (valued at $6.89M in the application), then stacking city gap money and 9% credits to go from award to occupancy in about 26 months.

status.label: Open: construction complete and residents moved in by end of August 2025
status.detail: Groundbreaking was on May 14, 2024, per Mile High CRE, after FirstBank closed a $21 million loan. BHP says construction finished in August 2025 (fall 2025 elsewhere on the same page) and residents had moved in by the end of August; open houses were held from 2025-08-27. Occupancy level and the CHFA placed-in-service date are not public.

next_step: Watch for CHFA's placed-in-service record and BHP board materials reporting lease-up and any work on the adjacent Trammell Crow parcel.

key_numbers.meaning: All income-restricted at 30% to 60% AMI in the award; five 30% AMI three-bedroom units are set aside for families experiencing or at risk of homelessness, with BHP project-based vouchers.
The full amount requested; about $14.5M over 10 years (inferred). BHP described the credits as worth up to $13 million.

key_numbers.meaning: Trammell Crow Residential conveyed the site to BHP to meet part of its Boulder inclusionary housing obligation; the city money (about $8.5M at 73 units, inferred) was planned in the application.

background.text: Diagonal Plaza is a long-declining shopping center site at 28th Street and Iris Avenue; in June 2021 Boulder City Council unanimously called up a concept plan from Trammell Crow Residential and BHP for nearly 200 homes, because the BC-1 zoning's open-space rule would have limited housing to about 50 to 60 units.

Trammell Crow Residential is redeveloping about five adjacent acres into workforce housing and retail (230 market-rate apartments, per BHP); BHP's 73 affordable homes and the existing Diagonal Court form a 103-unit BHP campus with a shared park.

Planning Board unanimously approved the Site Review at a public hearing before the application; the application said the project was fully entitled, with technical documents due in March 2023 and permits targeted by the end of 2023.

Cost drivers named in the application: the Boulder energy code (solar array, high-efficiency HVAC at about $7,500 a unit more, aerosol air sealing at $86,000), extra storage and bike parking (about $3,100 a unit) and rooftop equipment screening ($118,000).

Market study figures in the application: an affordable vacancy rate of about 1.0%, overall and 60% AMI capture rates above CHFA's 25% threshold, and expected lease-up of 30 units a month without concessions.
BHP won two competitive CHFA awards in 2023, the first time in its history: this 9% award and a 4% plus state credit award for the 100-unit Rally Apartments at 2727 29th Street.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's reports give the address as 3320 28th Street, BHP's 2023 release and BizWest give 2850 Iris Avenue, and BHP's current page gives 2950 and 2960 Hawthorn Avenue.
CHFA's award description sets incomes at 30% to 60% AMI (10 units at 30%), while BHP's current property and open-house pages describe Hawthorn Court as serving households at 40% to 60% AMI.
BHP and BizWest say the project won 9% federal and state housing tax credits, while CHFA's 2023 Round One award report lists only the federal 9% amount.
BHP's open-house notice describes 73 one- and two-bedroom homes, while CHFA and BHP's property page list six three-bedroom units.
